title: Rift
summary: RIFT, noun [from rive.] A cleft; a fissure; an opening made by riving or splitting. RIFT, verb transitive to cleave; to rive; to split; as, to rift an oak or a rock. RIFT, verb intransitive 1. to burs

inlines.v: RIFT, noun [from rive.] A cleft; a fissure; an opening made by riving or splitting. RIFT, verb transitive to cleave; to rive; to split; as, to rift an oak or a rock. RIFT, verb intransitive 1. to burst open; to split. Timber - not apt to rift with ordnance. 2. to belch; to break wind. [Local.]
